## Great work needs great people.

 Formidable helps founders, CEOs, and family offices find the leaders who build what lasts: the cities, industries, institutions, and living systems a good society runs on.

 What Formidable does

 Formidable is an executive search and talent consultancy. We recruit senior leaders, build teams, provide fractional executives, and design organizations for people whose work shapes public life.

 Who is Formidable for?
Founders, CEOs, boards, and family offices hiring executives in six sectors: built environment, manufacturing, climate, democracy reform, cozytech, and ecology. Searches are led by Nathaniel Koloc from Bedford, New York.

 Where we work

 A principle we hold

## Delegate the recruiting. Never the hiring.

 Finding candidates can be handed off. Choosing the person who will carry your mission cannot. Formidable runs the search so you can spend your time where it counts: on the final judgment.

 And every candidate, hired or not, should leave the process glad they took the call. How you treat the people you do not hire is your reputation in the market.

 FAQ

## Questions, answered

## What is Formidable?

Formidable is an executive search and talent consultancy. It recruits executives, builds teams, provides fractional C-suite leaders, and designs organizations for founders, CEOs, and family offices.

## Which sectors does Formidable work in?

Six: Built Environment & Urban Development, Manufacturing & Industrials, Climate & Resilience, Democracy Reform & Policy Innovation, Cozytech, and Ecology & Conservation.

## Who leads Formidable?

Nathaniel Koloc, an executive recruiting partner who has led more than 50 executive searches over the past decade and co-founded ReWork, an impact-careers company acquired by Koya Leadership Partners in 2018.

## How do I start a search?

Email hello@formidable.services with a few lines about the role and your organization. The first conversation is about what the role needs to accomplish.

## Building something meant to outlast you?

 Tell us about the role, the team, or the organization you are trying to build. Every conversation starts with what you want the work to leave behind.

 Email hello@formidable.services

# https://formidable.services/approach.html

Our Approach: Legacy, Mastery, Freedom | Formidable

 Skip to content

 Home / Approach
 Our approach

## Legacy. Mastery. Freedom.

 Three attributes of fulfilling work, in a deliberate order. It is how Nathaniel Koloc has thought about careers for more than a decade, and it is how Formidable runs a search.

 Start a conversation See services

 What is the Legacy, Mastery, Freedom framework?
A model of fulfilling work developed by Nathaniel Koloc. Pursue legacy first (the impact you want), build the mastery that impact requires, then exchange mastery for freedom: pay, flexibility, and choice. In short, legacy guides mastery, which unlocks freedom.

 1

## Legacy

 What will be better because of this work?

 A higher purpose: the world is better after the work is done. Legacy comes first, because it decides which work is worth mastering at all.

 2

## Mastery

 What craft will this person keep getting better at?

 The craft of getting better at the skills the legacy requires. Mastery is how good intentions turn into real results.

 3

## Freedom

 What choices does this role earn them?

 Choosing who you work with, what you work on, and where and when. Freedom is what mastery is exchanged for as a career advances.

 Why the order matters

## Start with what you want to leave behind.

 Most career advice, and most recruiting, starts at the wrong end. It leads with compensation and title (freedom) or with the skills on a résumé (mastery), and treats purpose as a nice-to-have.

 The order matters because each step makes the next one possible. Knowing the impact you want tells you which skills are worth mastering. Real mastery is what earns real freedom. Skip the first step and you can get very good at work that does not matter to you.

 Nathaniel's view is that the deepest career advantage comes from knowing what you want, not from piling up accomplishments. It is also why he has argued that "follow your passion" is incomplete advice: self-knowledge beats a résumé built by accident.

 In a search

## How the framework shapes the work.

 01

## Scope the role around its legacy
Before a single outreach, we define what the role must leave behind: the outcomes that will matter in five years, not just the bullet points that matter on day one.

 02

## Search the people who are not looking
The strongest candidates are usually busy doing great work. Reaching them takes relationships and a pitch that speaks to what they care about.

 03

## Evaluate for mastery
Track records are a start. We look for evidence of craft: how someone thinks, how they have grown, and how they make the people around them better.

 04

## Close on freedom
Great people choose where they work. We help you design an offer, from scope to compensation to flexibility, that a top candidate says yes to.

 Two commitments

## Hiring is the leader's job. Respect is everyone's.

 You decide. Recruiting can be delegated. Hiring cannot. Formidable brings you a short list of people worth your time and helps you judge them, but the decision stays with the leader who will live with it.

 Every candidate is treated well. Most people in a search will not get the job. Each of them should still come away respected and well informed, because that experience becomes your reputation.

 Success means helping people. Nathaniel's simplest rule: professional success comes down to how much you help other people. A good search helps the organization, the person hired, and the people who were not.

 FAQ

## Questions, answered

## Who created the Legacy, Mastery, Freedom framework?

Nathaniel Koloc, who leads Formidable. He has written about it in Harvard Business Review, including the 2013 piece "How to Build a Career Worth Having."

## How does the framework help employers, not just job seekers?

It gives an employer a better pitch and a better filter. Roles described in terms of legacy, mastery, and freedom attract people who want the work itself, and those people tend to stay and grow.

## Building something meant to outlast you?

 Tell us about the role, the team, or the organization you are trying to build. Every conversation starts with what you want the work to leave behind.

 Email hello@formidable.services

 Choosing

## Not sure which you need?

 One role, high stakes: executive search.

 Several roles that need to work together: a team build.

 A gap you need covered now: a fractional executive.

 Friction you cannot pin on any one person: org design, often followed by hiring.

 Most engagements start with a short conversation. It is fine not to know which one you need yet.

## Executive Search

 One critical hire, found with care and closed with conviction.

 Start a conversation How we think

 What is executive search at Formidable?
A senior hire changes the trajectory of an organization. Formidable runs executive searches for founders, CEOs, and family offices who need a leader to carry real responsibility, and who want the search done by someone who understands the work.

 A senior hire changes the trajectory of an organization. Formidable runs executive searches for founders, CEOs, and family offices who need a leader to carry real responsibility, and who want the search done by someone who understands the work.
Best for: Founders hiring their first executives, CEOs replacing or adding C-suite leaders, and family offices building operating teams.

 How it works

Team Builds: Hiring a Leadership Team at Once | Formidable

 Skip to content

 Home / Services / Team Builds
 Service II

## Team Builds

 Several hires at once, designed as a team, not a list.

 Start a conversation How we think

 What is team builds at Formidable?
Sometimes the need is not one person but a team: a new leadership bench after a raise, a function built from zero, or a spin-out that needs to be fully staffed. A team build treats those hires as one design problem.

 Sometimes the need is not one person but a team: a new leadership bench after a raise, a function built from zero, or a spin-out that needs to be fully staffed. A team build treats those hires as one design problem.
Best for: Organizations after a funding round, new ventures and spin-outs, and family offices standing up an operating company.

 How it works

## What the work looks like.

 01

## Design the team before the roles
Who decides what, who reports to whom, and which skills must overlap. Getting this right first saves painful reorganizations later.

 02

## Sequence the hires
The order matters. The first leader you hire often helps recruit the next, so we plan the sequence on purpose.

 03

## Hire for the whole
Each candidate is evaluated against the team they will join, not only against a job description.

 04

## Run it as one engagement
One partner, one process, and one consistent candidate experience across every role.

 FAQ

## Questions, answered

## What is a team build?

A team build is a single engagement in which Formidable designs and recruits several related roles together, such as a full leadership team or a new department, instead of running separate searches.

## Is a team build more efficient than separate searches?

Usually. Candidates see a coherent story about the team they are joining, and the design work is done once instead of role by role.

## Building something meant to outlast you?

 Tell us about the role, the team, or the organization you are trying to build. Every conversation starts with what you want the work to leave behind.

Fractional C-Suite Executives | Formidable

 Skip to content

 Home / Services / Fractional C-Suite
 Service III

## Fractional C-Suite

 Senior leadership now, while the permanent hire takes shape.

 Start a conversation How we think

 What is fractional c-suite at Formidable?
Not every organization is ready for a full-time executive on day one, and not every gap can wait for a search to finish. Fractional leadership puts experienced operators in the seat for a defined period.

 Not every organization is ready for a full-time executive on day one, and not every gap can wait for a search to finish. Fractional leadership puts experienced operators in the seat for a defined period.
Best for: Early-stage companies, organizations in transition, and teams covering an unexpected executive departure.

 How it works

## What the work looks like.

 01

## Operate immediately
A fractional leader steps into real responsibility: running a function, stabilizing a team, or leading a critical project.

 02

## Clarify the permanent role
Doing the job is the best way to define it. Fractional work often produces the clearest possible brief for the eventual full-time hire.

 03

## Right-size the commitment
Pay for the level of seniority you need, at the time and scale you need it.

 04

## Hand off cleanly
When the permanent leader arrives, they inherit a working function and a documented plan.

 FAQ

## Questions, answered

## What is a fractional executive?

A fractional executive is a senior leader who works part-time or for a fixed term, taking on real C-suite responsibility without a full-time permanent commitment.

## Can a fractional engagement turn into an executive search?

Yes. Many fractional engagements lead directly into a search for the permanent role, with a much sharper brief as a result.

## Building something meant to outlast you?

 Tell us about the role, the team, or the organization you are trying to build. Every conversation starts with what you want the work to leave behind.

# https://formidable.services/org-design.html

Organizational Design for Growing Organizations | Formidable

 Skip to content

 Home / Services / Organizational Design
 Service IV

## Organizational Design

 The structure that lets good people do great work.

 Start a conversation How we think

 What is organizational design at Formidable?
Most hiring problems are structure problems in disguise. Org design looks at roles, reporting lines, and decision rights so the people you have, and the people you hire next, can do their best work.

 Most hiring problems are structure problems in disguise. Org design looks at roles, reporting lines, and decision rights so the people you have, and the people you hire next, can do their best work.
Best for: Organizations from early stage to more than $100M in revenue that have outgrown their current structure.

 How it works

## What the work looks like.

 01

## Map the work, not the org chart
Start with what must get done and who should own it. Boxes and lines come last.

 02

## Set clear decision rights
Ambiguity about who decides is the most common source of friction in growing teams.

 03

## Plan the next stage
Design for the organization you are becoming, with a hiring roadmap to get there.

 04

## Connect structure to hiring
Every design produces a concrete list of roles, and Formidable can recruit them.

 Sectors

## Where we do this work.

 Built Environment & Urban Development
Manufacturing & Industrials
Climate & Resilience
Democracy Reform & Policy Innovation
Cozytech
Ecology & Conservation

 FAQ

## Questions, answered

## When does an organization need org design?

Common signals: decisions are slowing down, roles overlap, the founder is a bottleneck, or a new strategy needs a different team.

## What experience does Formidable bring to org design?

Nathaniel Koloc has led org design and team building for organizations from early stage to more than $100M in revenue, and has run companies of up to about $25M in revenue as a general manager.

## Building something meant to outlast you?

 Why these six

## The common thread.

 A park, a factory, a power grid, an election system, a community, a watershed. Each one is infrastructure in the broadest sense: something people rely on without thinking about it, and something that fails slowly and expensively when it is led badly.

 The sectors also share a talent problem. The best leaders in them are often driven by purpose and not actively looking. Reaching them takes a search built on what they care about, which is what the Legacy, Mastery, Freedom approach is for.

Executive Search for Built Environment & Urban Development | Formidable

 Home / Sectors / Built Environment
 Sector No. 01

## Built Environment & Urban Development

 Parks, waterfronts, housing, and the places where public life actually happens.

 Start a conversation How we think

 Does Formidable recruit in built environment?
Yes. Built Environment & Urban Development is one of Formidable's six core sectors. The firm runs executive searches, team builds, fractional C-suite placements, and org design for organizations in this field.

 Cities are the longest-running projects people undertake. The organizations that plan, build, and steward them, from public-private park conservancies to developers and planning advisors, need leaders who can hold a twenty-year vision and still ship this quarter.

 The leadership challenge

## What makes hiring here different.

## Long horizons, short tenures
A waterfront plan can outlive three executive directors. The leader you hire has to inherit a vision, improve it, and hand it on intact.

## Many masters
Boards, city agencies, neighbors, funders, and developers all have a claim on the work. The job is as much diplomacy as delivery.

## Public trust is the asset
In civic space, one bad hire costs more than a missed milestone. It costs goodwill that took a decade to earn.

 Roles

## Searches we are built for.

 Executive Director / CEO
Chief Operating Officer
Head of Development & Partnerships
VP of Planning & Design
Chief Program Officer
Head of Real Estate & Capital Projects

Urban Villages

## Questions, answered

## What kinds of built-environment organizations does Formidable work with?

Park and public-space conservancies, waterfront and coastal advocates, urban development and planning advisors, and mission-driven real estate developers. Past clients include The High Line, Waterfront Alliance, HR&A Advisors, and Urban Villages.

## Do you recruit for public-private partnerships?

Yes. Leaders who can work across a nonprofit board, city government, and private capital at the same time are rare, and finding them is a core part of this practice.

Executive Search for Manufacturing & Industrials | Formidable

 Skip to content

 Home / Sectors / Manufacturing
 Sector No. 02

## Manufacturing & Industrials

 Rebuilding the capacity to make things, at home and at scale.

 Start a conversation How we think

 Does Formidable recruit in manufacturing?
Yes. Manufacturing & Industrials is one of Formidable's six core sectors. The firm runs executive searches, team builds, fractional C-suite placements, and org design for organizations in this field.

 A country that cannot make things cannot keep its promises. The new wave of industrial companies, from materials recyclers to advanced manufacturers, need operators who understand both the factory floor and the cap table.

 The leadership challenge

## What makes hiring here different.

## Atoms are unforgiving
Software can be patched on Friday night. A production line cannot. Industrial leaders need judgment that only comes from having shipped physical product.

## Startup speed, plant discipline
Hard-tech founders need executives who move like a startup and run safety, quality, and supply chain like a seasoned plant manager.

## Scarce, specific talent
The people who have scaled a first-of-a-kind facility are a short list. Finding them takes relationships, not job boards.

 Roles

## Searches we are built for.

 Chief Operating Officer
VP of Manufacturing / Operations
Head of Supply Chain
Plant / Site Leader
Chief Commercial Officer
VP of Engineering

 Selected clients in this space

## Does Formidable recruit for early-stage hard-tech companies?

Yes. Founders building first-of-a-kind facilities are a natural fit. The work is finding operators who can scale production without losing startup speed.

## Can you help design the operations org, not just fill one role?

Yes. Team builds and org design are core services, so a single search can grow into a plan for the whole operations bench.

Climate & Resilience Executive Search | Formidable

 Home / Sectors / Climate
 Sector No. 03

## Climate & Resilience

 The companies and coalitions helping communities adapt, decarbonize, and endure.

 Start a conversation How we think

 Does Formidable recruit in climate?
Yes. Climate & Resilience is one of Formidable's six core sectors. The firm runs executive searches, team builds, fractional C-suite placements, and org design for organizations in this field.

 Climate work has moved from pledge to build-out. That shift needs a different kind of leader: someone who can raise capital, win permits, earn community trust, and run a durable organization through decades of change.

 The leadership challenge

## What makes hiring here different.

## From mission to machine
The climate sector is full of passion. What it needs now is execution: leaders who turn a good idea into an institution that compounds.

## Cross-sector fluency
The best climate executives speak policy, finance, and engineering. That combination is rare and worth searching hard for.

## Resilience is local
Adaptation happens in specific places with specific people. Leaders need to earn trust on the ground, not just in a deck.

 Roles

## Searches we are built for.

 Chief Executive Officer
Chief Operating Officer
Head of Policy & Government Affairs
Chief Revenue / Commercial Officer
Head of Project Development
Chief of Staff

## What kinds of climate organizations does Formidable serve?

Climate tech companies, resilience and adaptation firms, research nonprofits, and the coalitions that connect them. Past clients include The Resiliency Company, New Harvest, and Blue Whale Materials.

## Do you work with both nonprofits and for-profit companies?

Yes. Many of the most important climate organizations are hybrids, and leaders who can work across those models are a specialty.

 Sector No. 04

## Democracy Reform & Policy Innovation

 Organizations working to make self-government work better for everyone.

 Start a conversation How we think

 Does Formidable recruit in democracy reform?
Yes. Democracy Reform & Policy Innovation is one of Formidable's six core sectors. The firm runs executive searches, team builds, fractional C-suite placements, and org design for organizations in this field.

 Self-government is a craft, and like any craft it needs skilled people. Reform organizations, civic platforms, and policy shops need leaders who can grow a movement, run a disciplined organization, and earn trust across divides.

 The leadership challenge

## What makes hiring here different.

## Growth is the mission
In civic work, reach is impact. Leaders need to grow members, coalitions, and adoption with the rigor of a growth-stage company.

## Trust across lines
Nonpartisan work lives or dies on credibility. The right hire is respected by people who disagree with each other.

## Campaign tempo, institution patience
Election cycles demand speed, but reform takes decades. Leaders have to work at both speeds.

 Roles

## Searches we are built for.

 Executive Director / CEO
Chief Growth Officer
Chief Operating Officer
Head of Policy
VP of Coalitions & Partnerships
Chief Communications Officer

 Sector No. 05

## Cozytech

 Technology built to bring people closer, not to keep them scrolling.

 Start a conversation How we think

 Does Formidable recruit in cozytech?
Yes. Cozytech is one of Formidable's six core sectors. The firm runs executive searches, team builds, fractional C-suite placements, and org design for organizations in this field.

 Not every technology company should be optimized for attention. Cozytech is the growing set of products built around connection, belonging, and real life offline, and it needs leaders who can grow a business without turning users into a metric.

 The leadership challenge

## What makes hiring here different.

## Growth with a conscience
The hardest job in cozytech is scaling without adopting the tactics the category exists to reject.

## Product taste is strategy
In a category defined by how it feels, leaders need taste as much as they need dashboards.

## Community is the moat
The best cozytech companies are built with their users, not on top of them. Leaders need to earn that relationship.

 Roles

## Searches we are built for.

 Chief Executive Officer
Chief Product Officer
Head of Community
Chief Growth / Marketing Officer
Chief Operating Officer
Head of Trust & Safety

 FAQ

## Questions, answered

## What is cozytech?

Cozytech describes technology designed around human connection, belonging, and wellbeing: products meant to make life warmer and more social, rather than to maximize screen time.

## What leadership roles does a cozytech company need first?

Usually a product or growth leader who can scale the user base while protecting the experience. Formidable often pairs that search with org design so the second and third hires are planned too.

## Hiring in cozytech?

 Tell us about the role and what it needs to accomplish. We will tell you honestly whether we are the right fit.

 Sector No. 06

## Ecology & Conservation

 Protecting and restoring the living systems everything else depends on.

 Start a conversation How we think

 Does Formidable recruit in ecology?
Yes. Ecology & Conservation is one of Formidable's six core sectors. The firm runs executive searches, team builds, fractional C-suite placements, and org design for organizations in this field.

 Conservation works on the timescale of forests and watersheds. The organizations doing it need leaders who can raise durable capital, manage land and science, and build institutions that outlast any single campaign.

 The leadership challenge

## What makes hiring here different.

## Generational stewardship
A land trust or restoration project is a promise to people who are not born yet. Leadership has to be built for that.

## Science meets fundraising
Great conservation leaders translate ecology into a story donors, landowners, and agencies can act on.

## Partnership-heavy work
Results come from coalitions of landowners, governments, tribes, and funders. The leader is the connector.

 Roles

## Searches we are built for.

 Executive Director / President
Chief Conservation Officer
Head of Development
Chief Operating Officer
Director of Science
Head of Land & Stewardship

## Can you recruit leaders with both science and fundraising experience?

That combination is exactly what most conservation boards ask for, and it takes a targeted search to find.

# https://formidable.services/about.html

About Nathaniel Koloc | Formidable

 Skip to content

 Home / About
 About

## Nathaniel Koloc.

 Executive recruiting partner to founders, CEOs, and family offices, operating as Formidable from Bedford, New York.

 Start a conversation How we think

 Who is Nathaniel Koloc?
An executive recruiter and talent consultant who leads Formidable. He has led more than 50 executive searches, designed hiring systems that placed more than 12,000 people, co-founded the impact-careers company ReWork, and writes about hiring and meaningful work.

 Nathaniel has spent his career at the intersection of talent and purpose: helping people find meaningful work, and helping mission-driven organizations find the people who can carry it.

 In 2011 he co-founded ReWork with Evan Walden, as part of the Unreasonable Institute. ReWork connected impact-driven professionals with organizations creating measurable social and environmental impact, worked with more than 100 such organizations, and was covered by Harvard Business Review, Fast Company, and Forbes. In January 2018 it was acquired by Koya Leadership Partners.

 Since then he has worked as an executive recruiting partner, operator, and advisor. He has run companies of up to about $25M in revenue as a general manager, led org design from early stage to more than $100M in revenue, and been a principal on both the buy and sell side of M&A.

 Track record

## A decade of building teams.

 Search50+ executive searches over 10 years for founders, CEOs, and family offices.

 SystemsDesigned hiring systems that placed more than 12,000 people.

 OperatingGeneral manager of companies up to roughly $25M in revenue; org design from early stage to $100M+.

 CivicRan talent operations for a presidential campaign, chaired a 2018 New York State Senate race, and remains active in democracy reform.

 ExperiencesCreated "Scrimmages," day-long hackathons, along with multi-day accelerators and a 30-day residential personal accelerator; co-created the Super Age Games.

 EducationUniversity of Vermont.

 "...what a world would look like with abundant creative deployment of capital that clearly expresses a unique point of view for public benefit."

 Nathaniel Koloc, "The World Needs Your Great Work," Palladium Magazine, 2026

 Writing

## On hiring, careers, and great work.

 Nathaniel writes and speaks about hiring and talent in the purpose economy. His work has appeared in Harvard Business Review, Palladium Magazine, Entrepreneur, The Muse, and Quartz.

 Read selected writing 

 FAQ

## Questions, answered

## What was ReWork?

ReWork was an impact-careers company co-founded in 2011 by Nathaniel Koloc and Evan Walden. It connected professionals with organizations creating measurable social and environmental impact and was acquired by Koya Leadership Partners in January 2018.

## Where is Formidable based?

Formidable is based at 19 Jackson Road, Bedford, NY 10506, and works with clients across the United States.

# https://formidable.services/contact.html

Contact Formidable | Start an Executive Search

 Skip to content

 Home / Contact
 Get in touch

## Let's talk about the work.

 The best first message is short: who you are, what you are building, and the role or problem on your mind.

 Email

 hello@formidable.services
 Office

 19 Jackson RoadBedford, NY 10506
 Write to us 

## What to include

 Your organization, in a sentence or two.

 The need: a role, a team, interim cover, or a structure problem.

 What success looks like in a few years. This is the legacy question, and it shapes everything else.

 Timing, and anything that makes the search sensitive.

 Looking for your next role? Formidable recruits for client organizations rather than representing job seekers, but you are welcome to introduce yourself if your work fits one of the six sectors.

 FAQ

## Questions, answered

## How do I start working with Formidable?

Email hello@formidable.services with a short note about your organization and the need. The first step is a conversation, not a contract.

## Does Formidable work outside New York?

Yes. Formidable is based in Bedford, New York, and works with organizations across the United States.

## What size organizations does Formidable work with?

From early-stage ventures to organizations with more than $100M in revenue, as well as family offices and the operating companies they back.

## Does Formidable help job seekers find roles?

Formidable works on behalf of hiring organizations. Candidates whose experience fits one of the six sectors are welcome to get in touch.
